newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open firmer on tame U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open firmer on tame U.S. inflation.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger in active trade on Tuesday, strengthening in the wake of a report showing the U.S. consumer prices rose less than expected in March, dealers said.

"We're following the U.S.. The data was slightly favorable. We were better bid even prior to that. I think there's probably some short positions in the market that needed to be covered," said a T-bill dealer with one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.22 percent from 3.27 percent at Monday's close.

Canadian T-bills strengthened after the U.S. March consumer price index allayed market fears of an acceleration in price growth, sparking a rally in U.S. debt markets and easing the pressure on Federal Reserve policymakers to raise interest rates there.

Investors in Canadian T-bills are now looking ahead to the auction this afternoon of C$4.8 billion in three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills. Results of the auction will be released at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.44 percent from 3.58 percent on Friday.
The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 4.36 percent from 4.46 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
